articles.title: 5 snakes that hide in potted plants and gardens: From well-camouflaged snakes blending into potting soil to those that shelter among leaves and dense foliage, these snakes may be hard to spot around houseplants, balconies and home gardens
articles.description: Most of us picture snakes in forests or fields, not in the tulsi pot by the window. But gardens, balconies and plant-filled terraces offer cool shade, moist soil, hiding spots and plenty of insects, frogs and rodents to eat. Some snakes slip into these spaces without drawing any attention, and several blend so well with soil and leaves that they are easy to miss. Most are harmless and simply passing through, though a few are venomous. Here are five snakes that can hide around potted plants and home gardens, and what makes each one hard to spot.

articles.title: Colours that can calm your mind: Why certain shades make you feel more relaxed, how they influence your mood and which colours to bring into your home for a more soothing space
articles.description: Walk into a room painted in a soft sage green or a gentle sky blue, and your shoulders often drop before you even notice. Colour has a quiet way of shaping how we feel, which is why hospitals, spas and meditation studios tend to avoid loud, harsh shades. Researchers say the effect is real but not identical for everyone, since personal taste, culture and memories all play a part. Still, certain shades are widely linked with calm and comfort. Here is a five-part guide to how colour affects mood and which ones can make your home feel more soothing.
